9	## Chosen fix: Loop: seed file listing and auto-finish when full suite passes after an edit
10	
11	File: `mend/worker.py`
12	
13	In solve_task, make two changes.
14	(1) Seed the file listing. Before the while loop, compute `files = list_files(work)`. Build the first user message as `f"Bug report: {report}\n\nProject files:\n{files}"` so the model never spends a turn on list_files.
15	(2) Auto-finish on green.
16	- Track `edited = False`.
17	- In the tool-dispatch loop, set `edited = True` whenever an edit_file or write_file call returns without error.
18	- After building tool_results for a turn, check whether this turn contained a run_tests call with no pattern or an empty pattern whose result content starts with 'PASSED'. If it did and `edited` is True:
19	  - append the tool_results message as usual;
20	  - set result['stop'] = 'suite_passed';
21	  - set result['summary'] to the joined text blocks of that turn's assistant response, or 'Fixed the bug; full test suite passes.' if that text is empty;
22	  - return result immediately, without another model call.
23	Keep all other behaviour unchanged (MAX_TURNS, error handling, tool definitions).
24	
25	Why it is general: A passing unfiltered test suite is exactly the success criterion solve() uses. Any turn after it (re-reading, re-verifying, writing a summary) is pure overhead for every bug. All three traces spent 1-2 turns there, and prompt instructions alone did not stop the model. Giving the file listing up front also removes a mandatory orientation step on every task without assuming anything about the library.

2	
3	Manual tool-use loop (not the SDK's beta tool runner) so neatlogs' wrap() traces every
4	`messages.create` call and each tool call gets its own TOOL span.

6	The caller must run `neatlogs.init(...)` before calling `solve` (init must precede the
7	anthropic import, so the client is created lazily).

92	def _safe_path(work: Path, rel: str) -> Path:
93	    """Resolve a tool-supplied path, refusing anything outside the sandbox copy."""
94	    path = (work / rel).resolve()
95	    if not path.is_relative_to(work.resolve()):
96	        raise ValueError(f"path outside the project: {rel}")
97	    return path

100	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="list_files")
101	def list_files(work: Path) -> str:
102	    return "\n".join(
103	        str(p.relative_to(work)).replace("\\", "/")
104	        for p in sorted(work.rglob("*"))
105	        if p.is_file() and "__pycache__" not in p.parts
106	    )

109	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="read_file")
110	def read_file(work: Path, path: str, start: int = 1, lines: int = 200) -> str:
111	    text = _safe_path(work, path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
112	    chunk = text[start - 1 : start - 1 + lines]
113	    out = "\n".join(f"{start + i}\t{line}" for i, line in enumerate(chunk))
114	    remaining = len(text) - (start - 1 + len(chunk))
115	    if remaining > 0:
116	        out += f"\n... ({remaining} more lines; file has {len(text)} lines total)"
117	    return out

120	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="write_file")
121	def write_file(work: Path, path: str, content: str) -> str:
122	    target = _safe_path(work, path)
123	    if "tests" in target.relative_to(work.resolve()).parts:
124	        raise ValueError("editing tests is not allowed")
125	    target.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
126	    return f"wrote {path} ({len(content)} chars)"

129	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="edit_file")
130	def edit_file(work: Path, path: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
131	    target = _safe_path(work, path)
132	    if "tests" in target.relative_to(work.resolve()).parts:
133	        raise ValueError("editing tests is not allowed")
134	    text = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
135	    count = text.count(old)
136	    if count == 0:
137	        return _edit_ignoring_whitespace(target, path, text, old, new)
138	    if count > 1:
139	        raise ValueError(f"`old` occurs {count} times; include more surrounding context")
140	    target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")
141	    return f"edited {path}: replaced {old.count(chr(10)) + 1} line(s) with {new.count(chr(10)) + 1} line(s)"
142	
143	
144	def _indent(line: str) -> int:
145	    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
146	
147	
148	def _edit_ignoring_whitespace(target: Path, path: str, text: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
149	    """Fallback when `old` has no exact match: match line by line ignoring surrounding whitespace,
150	    re-indent `new` to fit, or explain precisely how `old` differs from the file."""
151	    old_lines = old.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
152	    file_lines = text.split("\n")
153	    stripped = [line.strip() for line in file_lines]
154	    want = [line.strip() for line in old_lines]
155	    n = len(old_lines)
156	    hits = [i for i in range(len(file_lines) - n + 1) if stripped[i : i + n] == want]
157	    if len(hits) > 1:
158	        starts = ", ".join(str(i + 1) for i in hits)
159	        raise ValueError(f"`old` matches (ignoring whitespace) at lines {starts}; include more surrounding context")
160	    first = next((k for k, w in enumerate(want) if w), None)
161	    if not hits:
162	        match = difflib.get_close_matches(want[first], stripped, n=1, cutoff=0) if first is not None else []
163	        if not match:
164	            raise ValueError("`old` not found in file; re-read the exact lines and copy them verbatim")
165	        line_no = stripped.index(match[0])
166	        actual, mine = file_lines[line_no], old_lines[first]
167	        raise ValueError(
168	            f"`old` not found. Closest line in the file is line {line_no + 1}: {actual!r} "
169	            f"(leading spaces: {_indent(actual)}); your first line was {mine!r} (leading spaces: {_indent(mine)}). "
170	            "Copy the text exactly as shown."
171	        )
172	    i = hits[0]
173	    delta = 0 if first is None else _indent(file_lines[i + first]) - _indent(old_lines[first])
174	    new_lines = new.rstrip("\n").split("\n") if new.rstrip("\n") else []
175	    if delta > 0:
176	        new_lines = [" " * delta + line if line.strip() else line for line in new_lines]
177	    elif delta < 0:
178	        new_lines = [line[min(-delta, len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))) :] for line in new_lines]
179	    file_lines[i : i + n] = new_lines
180	    target.write_text("\n".join(file_lines), encoding="utf-8")
181	    return (
182	        f"edited {path}: replaced {n} line(s) with {len(new_lines)} line(s) (note: your `old` had different "
183	        f"indentation than the file; matched ignoring whitespace and re-indented `new` by {delta:+d} spaces)"
184	    )
185	
186	
187	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="run_tests")
188	def run_tests_tool(work: Path, pattern: str = "") -> str:
189	    passed, output = run_tests(work, pattern)
190	    return f"{'PASSED' if passed else 'FAILED'}\n{output}"
191	
192	
193	HANDLERS = {"list_files": list_files, "read_file": read_file, "write_file": write_file, "edit_file": edit_file, "run_tests": run_tests_tool}

196	def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
197	    """The active neatlogs trace id, read from the W3C traceparent the SDK can inject."""
198	    carrier: dict[str, str] = {}
199	    if neatlogs.inject_trace_context(carrier) and "traceparent" in carrier:
200	        return carrier["traceparent"].split("-")[1]
201	    return None
202

204	@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")
205	def solve_task(task_id: str, report: str, work: Path) -> dict:
206	    """Run the agent loop on one task. Returns turns, tokens, stop reason and the trace id."""
207	    result = {"task_id": task_id, "trace_id": current_trace_id(), "turns": 0,
208	              "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "stop": None, "summary": ""}
209	    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": f"Bug report: {report}"}]
210	    system = PROMPT_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
211	    while result["turns"] < MAX_TURNS:
212	        result["turns"] += 1
213	        extra = {} if MODEL.startswith("claude-haiku-4-5") else {"output_config": {"effort": "medium"}}  # Haiku 4.5 rejects effort
214	        response = client().messages.create(
215	            model=MODEL, max_tokens=16000, system=system, tools=TOOLS, messages=messages, **extra,
216	        )
217	        result["input_tokens"] += response.usage.input_tokens
218	        result["output_tokens"] += response.usage.output_tokens
219	        result["stop"] = response.stop_reason
220	        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
221	        if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
222	            result["summary"] = next((b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), "")
223	            return result
224	        tool_results = []
225	        for block in response.content:
226	            if block.type != "tool_use":
227	                continue
228	            try:
229	                content, is_error = HANDLERS[block.name](work, **block.input), False
230	            except Exception as exc:  # report tool failures back to the model, don't crash the run
231	                content, is_error = f"Error: {exc}", True
232	            tool_results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id, "content": content, "is_error": is_error})
233	        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": tool_results})
234	    result["stop"] = "max_turns"
235	    return result
236

238	def solve(task: dict, work: Path) -> dict:
239	    """Solve one task in `work`, then judge it ourselves: pass = the full test suite passes."""
240	    started = time.time()
241	    result = solve_task(task["id"], task["report"], work)
242	    result["passed"], _ = run_tests(work)
243	    result["duration_s"] = round(time.time() - started, 1)
244	    return result

content.text:
I made the two changes in `solve_task` from the diagnosis's "Chosen fix" in `mend/worker.py`. I didn't touch any other file, and as you asked I haven't run anything, so the change is untested.

1. **File listing up front:** before the loop, `files = list_files(work)` is computed, and the first message is now `Bug report: {report}\n\nProject files:\n{files}`.
2. **Stop when the full suite passes:**
   - An `edited` flag starts as `False` and is set to `True` whenever an `edit_file` or `write_file` call succeeds.
   - Each turn also checks for a `run_tests` call with no pattern (or an empty one) whose result starts with `PASSED`.
   - If both are true, it adds that turn's tool results to the messages as usual, sets `stop='suite_passed'`, and returns straight away without another model call.
   - The summary is that turn's assistant text, or `"Fixed the bug; full test suite passes."` if the turn had no text.

The diagnosis didn't say what to put between text blocks when joining them, so I join them with nothing in between.

Everything else is unchanged.
